RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-women panel is not evidence of anything. Women are a large majority of teachers and school leaders in most systems, so such a panel is statistically unremarkable. Raising it signals you suspect bias rather than that you can show it, and it will undermine your credibility on the point that actually matters.

That point is strong: on paper you hold a master's in educational leadership and five years of actual leadership experience, against "courses" and classroom experience only. Press that. Send a written follow-up citing your earlier request, ask for the assessment criteria, their weighting, and the comparative scoring.

If the reasoning turns out to disregard your formal qualifications, you have a real case — on the merits, not on the panel's sex.
